children: ability to build personal relationships around the brand—the relational value—is a key and underappreciated component of the allure that is the Ferrari brand, says Morgan Stanley’s Edouard Aubin.

This relational value adds a fourth source of value to the more familiar components that include status, driving, and investment proposition, leading Aubin to become “increasingly positive on the strength of demand for Ferrari in the coming years.”

As such, Aubin maintains an Overweight rating and hikes his price target by 4% to $460, representing 15% upside to Wednesday’s closing price. His note and price target hike gave shares a boost on Thursday, putting Ferrari
in the plus column for the first time this week.

“Luxury consumption is typically associated with two sources of value,” Aubin argues. There is the symbolic value from Ferrari’s association with wealth, taste, achievement, and status, and experiential derived from the thrill of driving an iconic sportscar.

Then there are also arguably third and fourth sources of value: investment potential and relational value, the latter of which Aubin describes as the “access to a global community of like-minded owners and collectors, with Ferrari itself providing the infrastructure that brings this community together.” This, Aubin believes, creates another important driver of long-term demand.
“In our view, few luxury brands enable clients to build personal relationships around the brand to the same extent as Ferrari,” Aubin says.

Chief executive Benedetto Vigna seems to understand this dynamic and is capitalizing on the value of community events. Since becoming CEO in 2021, Ferrari’s client-engagement platform has expanded regional road and track activities and the launch of Ferrari Sport Prototipi Clienti for the 499P Modificata. The company has also increasingly combined product launches, racing, lifestyle, and hospitality within single events.

“In our view, the engagement platform has become a more structured client-lifecycle tool, intended to deepen loyalty, encourage collection building, and support repeat purchases while preserving exclusivity.”
Wall Street analysts agree with Aubin and share a Strong Buy outlook on Ferrari, while Seeking Alpha analysts view the stock as a Buy. Seeking Alpha’s Quant rating gives Ferrari
a Hold rating with a Quant score of 3.12 out of 5.

title: Ferrari's biggest asset may be the community behind it—Morgan Stanley
